course_rationale: BUS C150 Principles of Marketing replaces the mismatched Indian-history context. Domain: Marketing and Business. The five instructional modules regroup all 19 chapters of the attached OpenStax Principles of Marketing (2023), by Maria Gomez Albrecht, Mark Green, and Linda Hoffman: (1) Marketing Foundations and Strategy, chapters 1–2; (2) Markets, Buyer Behavior, Research, and Diversity, chapters 3–8; (3) Products, Innovation, Services, and Pricing, chapters 9–12; (4) Integrated Marketing Communications and Selling, chapters 13–16; (5) Distribution, Retailing, and Sustainable Marketing, chapters 17–19. The textbook itself uses three units; the five-module arrangement is an instructional adaptation. Definitions and evidence are grounded in the uploaded edition, with printed-page or section references. Misconceptions and diagnostic probes are authored pedagogical hypotheses, not claims that the textbook empirically documents student errors. Company examples, platform descriptions, statistics, and legal summaries retain their publication-era context and are not current-market or legal verification. Apparent source inconsistencies are flagged where relevant. The hierarchy represents teaching sections, glossary concepts, additional frameworks and competencies, indexed named examples, and applied assessment activities; noninstructional front matter, bibliographic entries, and repeated answer-key content are not independent concepts. Source attribution: Rice University / OpenStax, CC BY 4.0, https://openstax.org/details/books/principles-marketing. Access for free at openstax.org.

concepts.label: BUS C150 Principles of Marketing
concepts.definition: Explain, apply, analyze, evaluate, and design customer-value-oriented marketing across strategy, buyer behavior, research, offerings, communication, channels, and sustainability. The five modules are an adaptation of the attached textbook, not its original unit titles.

concepts.label: Marketing Foundations and Strategy
concepts.definition: Chapters 1–2: value creation, the marketing process and environment, customer relationships, strategic planning, portfolios, marketing plans, performance metrics, and ethics.

concepts.label: Markets, Buyer Behavior, Research, and Diversity
concepts.definition: Chapters 3–8: consumer and organizational decisions, segmentation, targeting and positioning, research and intelligence, global markets, diversity and inclusion.

concepts.label: Products, Innovation, Services, and Pricing
concepts.definition: Chapters 9–12: offerings and brands, product life cycles, innovation and adoption, services and quality, costs, demand, and pricing decisions.

concepts.label: Integrated Marketing Communications and Selling
concepts.definition: Chapters 13–16: communication and campaign planning, advertising, public relations, personal selling, promotion, direct and digital channels, and measurement.

concepts.label: Distribution, Retailing, and Sustainable Marketing
concepts.definition: Chapters 17–19: distribution channels, supply chains and logistics, retail and wholesale strategy, sustainability, stakeholder responsibility, and purpose.

concepts.label: Marketing and the Marketing Process
concepts.definition: Section 1.1, printed page 12, chapter 1 (Marketing and Customer Value). Learning outcomes: Define and describe marketing. Describe the benefits of marketing to the organization, its interested parties, and society. Explain the marketing process.

concepts.label: The Marketing Mix and the 4Ps of Marketing
concepts.definition: Section 1.2, printed page 18, chapter 1 (Marketing and Customer Value). Learning outcomes: Define and describe the marketing mix. List and explain the 4Ps of marketing.

concepts.label: Factors Comprising and Affecting the Marketing Environment
concepts.definition: Section 1.3, printed page 22, chapter 1 (Marketing and Customer Value). Learning outcomes: Define and describe the marketing environment. Explain the components of the marketing environment. Identify and describe the internal factors of the marketing environment. List and describe the components of the micro- and macroenvironments.

concepts.label: Evolution of the Marketing Concept
concepts.definition: Section 1.4, printed page 27, chapter 1 (Marketing and Customer Value). Learning outcomes: Describe the production concept. Define the product concept. Discuss the selling concept. Explain the marketing concept. Summarize the societal marketing concept and its features.

concepts.label: Determining Consumer Needs and Wants
concepts.definition: Section 1.5, printed page 30, chapter 1 (Marketing and Customer Value). Learning outcomes: Explain how an organization identifies consumer needs and wants. Describe the process through which an organization satisfies consumer needs and wants.

concepts.label: Customer Relationship Management (CRM)
concepts.definition: Section 1.6, printed page 33, chapter 1 (Marketing and Customer Value). Learning outcomes: Define customer relationship management (CRM). Describe the impact of CRM on customer loyalty and retention. Explain how CRM builds customer equity.

concepts.label: Ethical Marketing
concepts.definition: Section 1.7, printed page 35, chapter 1 (Marketing and Customer Value). Learning outcomes: Define ethical marketing. Describe the importance of ethical marketing. Explain the dos and don’ts of ethical marketing.

concepts.label: Developing a Strategic Plan
concepts.definition: Section 2.1, printed page 48, chapter 2 (Strategic Planning in Marketing). Learning outcomes: Define strategic planning and list the steps in the strategic planning process. Write an effective vision statement and mission statement. Describe the role of company values. Perform a gap analysis. Write SMART objectives and goals. Summarize ways to monitor progress of the strategic plan.

concepts.label: The Role of Marketing in the Strategic Planning Process
concepts.definition: Section 2.2, printed page 55, chapter 2 (Strategic Planning in Marketing). Learning outcomes: Explain the role of marketing in the strategic planning process. Discuss the business portfolio and identify planning tools. Describe a SWOT analysis. List and describe marketing strategies based on analytics.

concepts.label: Purpose and Structure of the Marketing Plan
concepts.definition: Section 2.3, printed page 64, chapter 2 (Strategic Planning in Marketing). Learning outcomes: Explain the purpose of a marketing plan. List and discuss elements that should be included in a marketing plan.

concepts.label: Marketing Plan Progress Using Metrics
concepts.definition: Section 2.4, printed page 72, chapter 2 (Strategic Planning in Marketing). Learning outcomes: Define marketing metrics. Explain key performance indicators (KPIs). Provide examples of business objective KPIs. Characterize sales/revenue generation KPIs. Provide examples of market share KPIs. Classify and discuss customer support KPIs.

concepts.label: Ethical Issues in Developing a Marketing Strategy
concepts.definition: Section 2.5, printed page 81, chapter 2 (Strategic Planning in Marketing). Learning outcomes: Explain the importance of ethical marketing. Describe key ethical considerations in strategic planning. Discuss examples of ethical companies.

concepts.label: Understanding Consumer Markets and Buying Behavior
concepts.definition: Section 3.1, printed page 94, chapter 3 (Consumer Markets and Purchasing Behavior). Learning outcomes: Define consumer buying behavior. Explain the nature of the buyer’s black box. Describe how consumer behavior is characterized into types.

concepts.label: Factors That Influence Consumer Buying Behavior
concepts.definition: Section 3.2, printed page 97, chapter 3 (Consumer Markets and Purchasing Behavior). Learning outcomes: List and describe the cultural factors that influence consumer buying behavior. Explain the social factors that impact consumer buying behavior. Discuss the personal factors that influence consumer buying behavior. Describe the psychological factors that influence consumer buying behavior. Explain situational factors that impact consumer buying behavior.

concepts.label: The Consumer Purchasing Decision Process
concepts.definition: Section 3.3, printed page 111, chapter 3 (Consumer Markets and Purchasing Behavior). Learning outcomes: Explain the first stage in the consumer purchasing decision process. Summarize the second stage in the consumer purchasing decision process. Describe the third stage in the consumer purchasing decision process. Discuss the fourth stage in the consumer purchasing decision process. Explain the fifth and final stage in the consumer purchasing decision process.

concepts.label: Ethical Issues in Consumer Buying Behavior
concepts.definition: Section 3.4, printed page 116, chapter 3 (Consumer Markets and Purchasing Behavior). Learning outcomes: Describe ethical issues related to consumer buying behavior. Identify the characteristics of an ethical consumer.

concepts.label: The Business-to-Business (B2B) Market
concepts.definition: Section 4.1, printed page 128, chapter 4 (Business Markets and Purchasing Behavior). Learning outcomes: Define the business-to-business (B2B) market. Distinguish characteristics of the B2B market versus the business-to-consumer (B2C) market.

concepts.label: Buyers and Buying Situations in a B2B Market
concepts.definition: Section 4.2, printed page 131, chapter 4 (Business Markets and Purchasing Behavior). Learning outcomes: Identify the types of buyers involved in the B2B market. Describe the types of buying situations that exist in the B2B market. List and describe the parties who participate in the B2B buying process.

concepts.label: Major Influences on B2B Buyer Behavior
concepts.definition: Section 4.3, printed page 138, chapter 4 (Business Markets and Purchasing Behavior). Learning outcomes: List and describe the external influences on B2B buyer behavior. Explain the internal factors that influence B2B buyer behavior. Examine the individual factors that impact B2B buyer behavior. List and describe the interpersonal factors that influence B2B buyer behavior. Explain the conditional factors that impact B2B buyer behavior.

concepts.label: Stages in the B2B Buying Process
concepts.definition: Section 4.4, printed page 141, chapter 4 (Business Markets and Purchasing Behavior). Learning outcomes: Explain and describe the stages in the B2B buying process.

concepts.label: Ethical Issues in B2B Marketing
concepts.definition: Section 4.5, printed page 144, chapter 4 (Business Markets and Purchasing Behavior). Learning outcomes: Discuss ethical issues pertaining to B2B marketing. Explain the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act. Provide an example of a company that displays ethics in B2B marketing.

concepts.label: Market Segmentation and Consumer Markets
concepts.definition: Section 5.1, printed page 156, chapter 5 (Market Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning). Learning outcomes: Define market segmentation. Describe the benefits of market segmentation. Discuss methods of segmenting consumer markets.

concepts.label: Segmentation of B2B Markets
concepts.definition: Section 5.2, printed page 165, chapter 5 (Market Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning). Learning outcomes: Describe the challenges of segmenting B2B markets. Discuss the advantages of segmenting B2B markets. Explain methods of segmenting B2B markets.

concepts.label: Segmentation of International Markets
concepts.definition: Section 5.3, printed page 169, chapter 5 (Market Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning). Learning outcomes: Describe the challenges of segmenting international markets. Discuss the advantages of segmenting international markets. Explain methods of segmenting international markets.

concepts.label: Essential Factors in Effective Market Segmentation
concepts.definition: Section 5.4, printed page 174, chapter 5 (Market Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning). Learning outcomes: List and describe the essential factors in effective market segmentation.

concepts.label: Selecting Target Markets
concepts.definition: Section 5.5, printed page 175, chapter 5 (Market Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning). Learning outcomes: Define target market. Explain target market strategies.

concepts.label: Product Positioning
concepts.definition: Section 5.6, printed page 181, chapter 5 (Market Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning). Learning outcomes: Define product positioning. Explain approaches to product positioning. Describe the positioning statement and perceptual maps.

concepts.label: Ethical Concerns and Target Marketing
concepts.definition: Section 5.7, printed page 186, chapter 5 (Market Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning). Learning outcomes: Discuss ethical implications of target market selection. Provide an example of a company that displays ethics in target marketing.

concepts.label: Marketing Research and Big Data
concepts.definition: Section 6.1, printed page 198, chapter 6 (Marketing Research and Market Intelligence). Learning outcomes: Define marketing research. Explain how marketing information provides an understanding of the customer and the marketplace. Explain the role of big data and the marketing information system.

concepts.label: Sources of Marketing Information
concepts.definition: Section 6.2, printed page 201, chapter 6 (Marketing Research and Market Intelligence). Learning outcomes: Identify sources of marketing information. Describe the different categories of marketing information.

concepts.label: Steps in a Successful Marketing Research Plan
concepts.definition: Section 6.3, printed page 203, chapter 6 (Marketing Research and Market Intelligence). Learning outcomes: Identify and describe the steps in a marketing research plan. Discuss the different types of data research. Explain how data is analyzed. Discuss the importance of effective research reports.

concepts.label: Ethical Issues in Marketing Research
concepts.definition: Section 6.4, printed page 216, chapter 6 (Marketing Research and Market Intelligence). Learning outcomes: Describe ethical issues relating to marketing research. Discuss ways to avoid unethical research practices.

concepts.label: The Global Market and Advantages of International Trade
concepts.definition: Section 7.1, printed page 228, chapter 7 (Marketing in a Global Environment). Learning outcomes: Define global market opportunities. Explain why international trade is advantageous to business. Discuss the challenges of international trade.

concepts.label: Assessment of Global Markets for Opportunities
concepts.definition: Section 7.2, printed page 232, chapter 7 (Marketing in a Global Environment). Learning outcomes: Identify the different ways marketers can assess opportunity in global markets. Discuss effective methods of analyzing global opportunities.

concepts.label: Entering the Global Arena
concepts.definition: Section 7.3, printed page 241, chapter 7 (Marketing in a Global Environment). Learning outcomes: List the strategies used in global competition. Discuss the different forms of global competition.

concepts.label: Marketing in a Global Environment
concepts.definition: Section 7.4, printed page 243, chapter 7 (Marketing in a Global Environment). Learning outcomes: Describe how marketing strategies are adapted for a global marketplace. Summarize how global strategies affect the 4Ps of marketing.

concepts.label: Ethical Issues in the Global Marketplace
concepts.definition: Section 7.5, printed page 247, chapter 7 (Marketing in a Global Environment). Learning outcomes: Identify ethical issues facing global organizations. Provide an example of a company that displays ethics in the global marketplace.

concepts.label: Strategic Marketing: Standardization versus Adaptation
concepts.definition: Section 8.1, printed page 260, chapter 8 (Marketing in a Diverse Marketplace). Learning outcomes: Define marketing standardization. Define marketing adaptation. Explain when to use diversity marketing as an adaptation strategy.

concepts.label: Diversity and Inclusion Marketing
concepts.definition: Section 8.2, printed page 263, chapter 8 (Marketing in a Diverse Marketplace). Learning outcomes: Define diversity marketing, multicultural marketing, and sociodemographic marketing. Explain why diversity marketing is needed in today’s marketplace. Explain the importance of diversity in market research. List the factors that impact diversity marketing.

concepts.label: Multicultural Marketing
concepts.definition: Section 8.3, printed page 271, chapter 8 (Marketing in a Diverse Marketplace). Learning outcomes: Define culture. Explain the difference between tangible and intangible cultural objectives. List the main elements through which culture is expressed. Describe Hofstede’s cultural dimensions.

concepts.label: Marketing to Hispanic, Black, and Asian Consumers
concepts.definition: Section 8.4, printed page 278, chapter 8 (Marketing in a Diverse Marketplace). Learning outcomes: Describe the Hispanic, Black, and Asian identities. Define acculturation. Explain how identity-related characteristics and factors connect Hispanic, Black, and Asian consumers. Describe how to market to Hispanic, Black, and Asian consumers.

concepts.label: Marketing to Sociodemographic Groups
concepts.definition: Section 8.5, printed page 287, chapter 8 (Marketing in a Diverse Marketplace). Learning outcomes: Define sociodemographic marketing. Explain how to market to the LGBTQIA+ community. Explain how to market based on generational differences. Explain how to market to consumers with disabilities. Describe how sociodemographic trends will impact future marketing.

concepts.label: Ethical Issues in Diversity Marketing
concepts.definition: Section 8.6, printed page 294, chapter 8 (Marketing in a Diverse Marketplace). Learning outcomes: Identify the ethical issues related to diversity marketing. Discuss how to address different consumer values to reduce issues in marketing.

concepts.label: Products, Services, and Experiences
concepts.definition: Section 9.1, printed page 308, chapter 9 (Products: Consumer Offerings). Learning outcomes: Differentiate between products, services, and experiences. Describe how consumer and business/industrial products are classified. Identify the four levels of a product.

concepts.label: Product Items, Product Lines, and Product Mixes
concepts.definition: Section 9.2, printed page 313, chapter 9 (Products: Consumer Offerings). Learning outcomes: Define product items, product lines, and product mixes. Describe product line length and depth. Discuss product line filling and product line stretching.

concepts.label: The Product Life Cycle
concepts.definition: Section 9.3, printed page 316, chapter 9 (Products: Consumer Offerings). Learning outcomes: Define the product life cycle. List and describe the stages of the product life cycle.

concepts.label: Marketing Strategies at Each Stage of the Product Life Cycle
concepts.definition: Section 9.4, printed page 318, chapter 9 (Products: Consumer Offerings). Learning outcomes: Discuss marketing strategies in the introduction stage of the product life cycle. Classify marketing strategies used in the growth stage of the product life cycle. Characterize marketing strategies used in the maturity stage of the product life cycle. Identify marketing strategies used in the decline stage of the product life cycle.

concepts.label: Branding and Brand Development
concepts.definition: Section 9.5, printed page 320, chapter 9 (Products: Consumer Offerings). Learning outcomes: Define branding and discuss its benefits. Discuss ways in which an organization can build strong brands.

concepts.label: Forms of Brand Development, Brand Loyalty, and Brand Metrics
concepts.definition: Section 9.6, printed page 325, chapter 9 (Products: Consumer Offerings). Learning outcomes: Identify branding strategies. Describe degrees of brand loyalty. Discuss metrics that can be used to measure brand strength and value.

concepts.label: Creating Value through Packaging and Labeling
concepts.definition: Section 9.7, printed page 329, chapter 9 (Products: Consumer Offerings). Learning outcomes: Describe how an organization creates value through packaging and labeling. Explain how packaging is used as a marketing tool.

concepts.label: Environmental Concerns Regarding Packaging
concepts.definition: Section 9.8, printed page 332, chapter 9 (Products: Consumer Offerings). Learning outcomes: Describe environmental concerns with respect to product packaging. Discuss strategies that are being used to address environmental concerns.

concepts.label: Ethical Issues in Packaging
concepts.definition: Section 9.9, printed page 335, chapter 9 (Products: Consumer Offerings). Learning outcomes: Explain ethical issues with respect to product packaging. Discuss product safety and ethical packaging trends.

concepts.label: New Products from a Customer’s Perspective
concepts.definition: Section 10.1, printed page 344, chapter 10 (Maintaining a Competitive Edge with New Offerings). Learning outcomes: Define a new product. Explain “newness” from the perspective of the customer. Explain the risks and rewards of developing new products.

concepts.label: Stages of the New Product Development Process
concepts.definition: Section 10.2, printed page 349, chapter 10 (Maintaining a Competitive Edge with New Offerings). Learning outcomes: Identify the stages of the new product development process. Define and describe the important factors of each stage of development.

concepts.label: The Use of Metrics in Evaluating New Products
concepts.definition: Section 10.3, printed page 353, chapter 10 (Maintaining a Competitive Edge with New Offerings). Learning outcomes: Explain the importance of establishing new product metrics. Describe metrics used to evaluate the success or failure of new products.

concepts.label: Factors Contributing to the Success or Failure of New Products
concepts.definition: Section 10.4, printed page 356, chapter 10 (Maintaining a Competitive Edge with New Offerings). Learning outcomes: Identify and discuss factors that contribute to the success of a new product. Identify and discuss factors that contribute to the failure of a new product.

concepts.label: Stages in the Consumer Adoption Process for New Products
concepts.definition: Section 10.5, printed page 361, chapter 10 (Maintaining a Competitive Edge with New Offerings). Learning outcomes: Describe the stages in the adoption process for new products. Identify and define new product adopter categories.

concepts.label: Ethical Considerations in New Product Development
concepts.definition: Section 10.6, printed page 364, chapter 10 (Maintaining a Competitive Edge with New Offerings). Learning outcomes: Discuss violations of patents, trademarks, and/or copyrights. Describe ways to exercise due care in product development.

concepts.label: Classification of Services
concepts.definition: Section 11.1, printed page 376, chapter 11 (Services: The Intangible Product). Learning outcomes: Define services. List the classification of services. Describe the characteristics of services.

concepts.label: The Service-Profit Chain Model and the Service Marketing Triangle
concepts.definition: Section 11.2, printed page 383, chapter 11 (Services: The Intangible Product). Learning outcomes: Define and explain the purpose of the service-profit chain model. Describe the steps in the service-profit chain model. Explain the Services Marketing Triangle.

concepts.label: The Gap Model of Service Quality
concepts.definition: Section 11.3, printed page 390, chapter 11 (Services: The Intangible Product). Learning outcomes: Describe the Gap Model of Service Quality. List and describe the dimensions of service quality.

concepts.label: Ethical Considerations in Providing Services
concepts.definition: Section 11.4, printed page 395, chapter 11 (Services: The Intangible Product). Learning outcomes: Describe the ethical considerations in providing services to customers. Discuss how ethics contribute to customer satisfaction.

concepts.label: Pricing and Its Role in the Marketing Mix
concepts.definition: Section 12.1, printed page 406, chapter 12 (Pricing Products and Services). Learning outcomes: Define pricing. Explain pricing and its role in the marketing mix. Explain the psychology of pricing.

concepts.label: The Five Critical Cs of Pricing
concepts.definition: Section 12.2, printed page 411, chapter 12 (Pricing Products and Services). Learning outcomes: List the five critical Cs of pricing. Characterize the five critical Cs of pricing.

concepts.label: The Five-Step Procedure for Establishing Pricing Policy
concepts.definition: Section 12.3, printed page 415, chapter 12 (Pricing Products and Services). Learning outcomes: List the five-step procedure for establishing pricing policy. Describe ways to determine the pricing objective. Identify ways to estimate demand. List ways to estimate costs. Explain how to analyze the external environment. Discuss selecting pricing strategies or tactics.

concepts.label: Pricing Strategies for New Products
concepts.definition: Section 12.4, printed page 423, chapter 12 (Pricing Products and Services). Learning outcomes: List the pricing strategies for new products. Explain each pricing strategy for new products.

concepts.label: Pricing Strategies and Tactics for Existing Products
concepts.definition: Section 12.5, printed page 425, chapter 12 (Pricing Products and Services). Learning outcomes: List the pricing strategies and tactics for existing products. Provide examples of each pricing strategy and tactic.

concepts.label: Ethical Considerations in Pricing
concepts.definition: Section 12.6, printed page 427, chapter 12 (Pricing Products and Services). Learning outcomes: Identify ethical issues related to the pricing of products and services. Describe the different types of unethical practices.

concepts.label: The Promotion Mix and Its Elements
concepts.definition: Section 13.1, printed page 438, chapter 13 (Integrated Marketing Communications). Learning outcomes: Define the promotion mix and explain its importance. List and describe the elements of the promotion mix.

concepts.label: The Communication Process
concepts.definition: Section 13.2, printed page 446, chapter 13 (Integrated Marketing Communications). Learning outcomes: Describe the communication process. Identify and discuss each element of the communication process.

concepts.label: Integrated Marketing Communications
concepts.definition: Section 13.3, printed page 450, chapter 13 (Integrated Marketing Communications). Learning outcomes: Define integrated marketing communications (IMC). Discuss why IMC is important in marketing.

concepts.label: Steps in the IMC Planning Process
concepts.definition: Section 13.4, printed page 453, chapter 13 (Integrated Marketing Communications). Learning outcomes: List the steps in the IMC planning process. Summarize the details of each step in IMC planning.

concepts.label: Ethical Issues in Marketing Communication
concepts.definition: Section 13.5, printed page 464, chapter 13 (Integrated Marketing Communications). Learning outcomes: Identify ethical issues with respect to marketing communications. Discuss ways to maintain and foster ethical marketing communications.

concepts.label: Advertising in the Promotion Mix
concepts.definition: Section 14.1, printed page 474, chapter 14 (The Promotion Mix: Advertising and Public Relations). Learning outcomes: Define advertising and provide examples. Discuss the importance of advertising in the promotion mix.

concepts.label: Major Decisions in Developing an Advertising Plan
concepts.definition: Section 14.2, printed page 477, chapter 14 (The Promotion Mix: Advertising and Public Relations). Learning outcomes: List the steps involved in developing an advertising plan. Describe the details involved in each step of advertising development. Discuss methods for assessing and evaluating the advertising program.

concepts.label: The Use of Metrics to Measure Advertising Campaign Effectiveness
concepts.definition: Section 14.3, printed page 485, chapter 14 (The Promotion Mix: Advertising and Public Relations). Learning outcomes: List the key performance indicators (KPIs) for measuring the effectiveness of an advertising campaign. Describe how each KPI is measured.

concepts.label: Public Relations and Its Role in the Promotion Mix
concepts.definition: Section 14.4, printed page 488, chapter 14 (The Promotion Mix: Advertising and Public Relations). Learning outcomes: Define public relations and discuss its role in the promotion mix. List and describe the tools of public relations.

concepts.label: The Advantages and Disadvantages of Public Relations
concepts.definition: Section 14.5, printed page 492, chapter 14 (The Promotion Mix: Advertising and Public Relations). Learning outcomes: Discuss the advantages of public relations. Discuss the disadvantages of public relations.

concepts.label: Ethical Concerns in Advertising and Public Relations
concepts.definition: Section 14.6, printed page 494, chapter 14 (The Promotion Mix: Advertising and Public Relations). Learning outcomes: Illustrate ethical issues with respect to advertising. Illustrate ethical issues with respect to public relations.

concepts.label: Personal Selling and Its Role in the Promotion Mix
concepts.definition: Section 15.1, printed page 506, chapter 15 (The Promotion Mix: Personal Selling and Sales Promotion). Learning outcomes: Define personal selling. Discuss the role of personal selling in the promotion mix.

concepts.label: Classifications of Salespeople Involved in Personal Selling
concepts.definition: Section 15.2, printed page 508, chapter 15 (The Promotion Mix: Personal Selling and Sales Promotion). Learning outcomes: List the various roles involved in personal selling. Describe the differences between the various personal selling roles.

concepts.label: Steps in the Personal Selling Process
concepts.definition: Section 15.3, printed page 511, chapter 15 (The Promotion Mix: Personal Selling and Sales Promotion). Learning outcomes: List the steps in the personal selling process. Describe each step in the personal selling process.

concepts.label: Management of the Sales Force
concepts.definition: Section 15.4, printed page 516, chapter 15 (The Promotion Mix: Personal Selling and Sales Promotion). Learning outcomes: Identify the issues involved in managing a sales force. List the various ways a sales force can be structured. Describe the tasks involved in sales force recruitment and selection. Discuss key metrics that can be used to assess sales performance. Describe the tasks involved in supervising and evaluating a sales force. Summarize the metrics that can be used for sales force performance evaluation.

concepts.label: Sales Promotion and Its Role in the Promotion Mix
concepts.definition: Section 15.5, printed page 521, chapter 15 (The Promotion Mix: Personal Selling and Sales Promotion). Learning outcomes: Define sales promotion. Discuss the importance of sales promotion in the promotion mix.

concepts.label: Main Types of Sales Promotion
concepts.definition: Section 15.6, printed page 525, chapter 15 (The Promotion Mix: Personal Selling and Sales Promotion). Learning outcomes: Discuss the primary types of consumer-oriented sales promotion. Discuss the primary types of trade-oriented sales promotion.

concepts.label: Ethical Issues in Personal Selling and Sales Promotion
concepts.definition: Section 15.7, printed page 529, chapter 15 (The Promotion Mix: Personal Selling and Sales Promotion). Learning outcomes: Discuss the ethical issues that may arise in personal selling. Discuss the ethical issues that may arise in sales promotion.

concepts.label: Traditional Direct Marketing
concepts.definition: Section 16.1, printed page 540, chapter 16 (Direct, Online, Social Media, and Mobile Marketing). Learning outcomes: List and describe the various forms of traditional direct marketing. Explain how the digital age has impacted direct marketing.

concepts.label: Social Media and Mobile Marketing
concepts.definition: Section 16.2, printed page 550, chapter 16 (Direct, Online, Social Media, and Mobile Marketing). Learning outcomes: Discuss social media marketing and its opportunities and challenges. Discuss mobile marketing and its opportunities and challenges.

concepts.label: Metrics Used to Evaluate the Success of Online Marketing
concepts.definition: Section 16.3, printed page 560, chapter 16 (Direct, Online, Social Media, and Mobile Marketing). Learning outcomes: Discuss the role of marketing metrics in digital, online, social media, and mobile marketing. List and describe the metrics used to evaluate the success of online marketing.

concepts.label: Ethical Issues in Digital Marketing and Social Media
concepts.definition: Section 16.4, printed page 566, chapter 16 (Direct, Online, Social Media, and Mobile Marketing). Learning outcomes: Describe ethical issues with respect to digital marketing and social media. Explain why ethical issues exist.

concepts.label: The Use and Value of Marketing Channels
concepts.definition: Section 17.1, printed page 576, chapter 17 (Distribution: Delivering Customer Value). Learning outcomes: Describe the use of marketing channels. Identify the different types of marketing channels. Discuss how marketing intermediaries add value to products.

concepts.label: Types of Marketing Channels
concepts.definition: Section 17.2, printed page 582, chapter 17 (Distribution: Delivering Customer Value). Learning outcomes: Identify the types of marketing channels that exist for consumer products. Describe the types of marketing channels that exist for business/industrial products. Discuss vertical, horizontal, multichannel, and omnichannel marketing systems.

concepts.label: Factors Influencing Channel Choice
concepts.definition: Section 17.3, printed page 587, chapter 17 (Distribution: Delivering Customer Value). Learning outcomes: Identify the factors that influence channel choice in distribution. Describe the different types of target market coverage. Discuss the buyer requirements influencing channel choice. Explain the product-related factors influencing channel choice. Describe the cost factors influencing channel choice.

concepts.label: Managing the Distribution Channel
concepts.definition: Section 17.4, printed page 593, chapter 17 (Distribution: Delivering Customer Value). Learning outcomes: Describe how channel members are selected. Explain how channel members are managed and motivated. Discuss how channel conflict is handled. Summarize the metrics used for channel member evaluation.

concepts.label: The Supply Chain and Its Functions
concepts.definition: Section 17.5, printed page 597, chapter 17 (Distribution: Delivering Customer Value). Learning outcomes: Define supply chain management (SCM). Explain the role of marketing in supply chain management. Describe the various functions of supply chain management.

concepts.label: Logistics and Its Functions
concepts.definition: Section 17.6, printed page 599, chapter 17 (Distribution: Delivering Customer Value). Learning outcomes: Define and describe logistics. Explain the functions of logistics. Describe logistics information management. Describe integrated logistics management. Characterize third-party logistics (3PL) providers.

concepts.label: Ethical Issues in Supply Chain Management
concepts.definition: Section 17.7, printed page 603, chapter 17 (Distribution: Delivering Customer Value). Learning outcomes: Discuss the issue of the carbon footprint versus the speed of shipping. Discuss the issue of sourcing sustainably.

concepts.label: Retailing and the Role of Retailers in the Distribution Channel
concepts.definition: Section 18.1, printed page 612, chapter 18 (Retailing and Wholesaling). Learning outcomes: Define retailing. Discuss the functions of retailers in the distribution channel.

concepts.label: Major Types of Retailers
concepts.definition: Section 18.2, printed page 617, chapter 18 (Retailing and Wholesaling). Learning outcomes: Characterize various store retailers. Characterize various non-store retailers

concepts.label: Retailing Strategy Decisions
concepts.definition: Section 18.3, printed page 626, chapter 18 (Retailing and Wholesaling). Learning outcomes: Describe how pricing affects retail strategy decisions. Explain how location is a factor in retail strategy decisions. Discuss the importance of retailer communications. Explain how merchandise affects retail strategy decisions.

concepts.label: Recent Trends in Retailing
concepts.definition: Section 18.4, printed page 632, chapter 18 (Retailing and Wholesaling). Learning outcomes: List major trends and developments in retailing. Discuss the reason for these trends and developments.

concepts.label: Wholesaling
concepts.definition: Section 18.5, printed page 635, chapter 18 (Retailing and Wholesaling). Learning outcomes: Define wholesaling. Identify different types of wholesalers.

concepts.label: Analyze Nabisco in its marketing context
concepts.definition: Identify Nabisco and analyze its role in the textbook's treatment of forms of brand development, brand loyalty, and brand metrics. Source: printed page 326. Evidence excerpt: Multibrands are new brand names within a company’s existing product category. For example, Nabisco manufactures various cookies within a product line but is marketed with different brand names. In this case, Chips Ahoy, Oreo, and Teddy Grahams all have brand equity on their own and do not need the benefit of the Nabisco brand. Each of these brands has a significant market share, so there is a benefit to retaining a multibranding approach. However, a multibranding approach does not work when the products have a small market share or fail to gain favorable retail shelf space to encourage sales.

Are you comfortable in your skin? In her TED Talk, Harvard professor Amy Cuddy discusses how body language impacts how others perceive you. Our nonverbals give others a perception about who we are and how we are feeling. Our body language conveys dominance, much like animals do to show their power. Our posture and the space that we take up signals confidence. But sometimes we take cues from others. If our conversation partner is showing dominance, our body language might shrink in response. concepts.label: Ch. 19 Building Your Personal Brand, task 1: A workplace study by Blue Beyond Consulting shows that 8 in 10 employees say that it’s…
concepts.definition: Source assessment in chapter 19, Building Your Personal Brand, task 1. Learner task: A workplace study by Blue Beyond Consulting shows that 8 in 10 employees say that it’s important that their employer’s values align with their values. Furthermore, more than 75 percent of respondents indicated that they expect their employer and business to be a force for good.31 Consider what you value and how you would like your future employer to honor those values. Research a few organizations to find an employer that closely aligns with your values. Write about how you might integrate your personal purpose with that of your employer to make the change that you wish to see in the world.

prerequisites.rationale: Consumer decision analysis requires understanding the benefits and sacrifices customers evaluate.
Segmentation requires a customer-needs orientation before grouping customers for different offers.
Adapting four-P decisions abroad requires identifying what each marketing-mix decision controls.
Identifying the benefit customers buy requires the prior distinction between value and the physical offering.
Relationship selling develops the foundational understanding of customer information and retention.
A research problem must be framed against the business decision and objective it is intended to inform.
Selecting advertising indicators requires first linking measurable performance to a defined objective.
Campaign acquisition-cost analysis requires distinguishing acquisition expenditure from exposure and activity.
New-product adoption applies the prior distinction between awareness, evaluation, purchase, and later behavior.
Explaining decoding errors requires understanding that receivers actively interpret information.
Interpreting potential advertising exposure requires distinguishing exposure from actual attention.
Post-sale follow-up requires understanding why customers can experience doubt after commitment.
Designing a team account approach requires identifying multiple organizational buying roles.
Linking upstream supply requirements to downstream customers requires understanding derived demand.
An integrated communication plan must know whose response it is designed to influence.
Brand positioning depends on understanding desired customer perceptions relative to alternatives.
Value-based pricing requires knowing which attributes drive the target buyer’s evaluation.
Assessing distribution coverage requires a defined target customer group.
Interpreting advertising sales tests requires distinguishing a causal effect from coincident sales.
Designing concept tests requires understanding project-specific customer evidence.
Generalizing pretest responses requires knowing which audience the sampled respondents represent.
Cross-cultural communication requires understanding how culturally situated meanings shape interpretation.
Retail markup analysis requires first separating sales, cost of goods, and profit ratios.
Assessing lifecycle environmental responsibility requires understanding material circulation and waste.
Constructing benefit-based appeals requires identifying the customer-perceived advantage over alternatives.
Selecting service distribution arrangements requires understanding that unused service capacity cannot be inventoried.
Retail location economics requires distinguishing recurring fixed commitments from sales-dependent costs.
Evaluating the profitability of sales incentives requires recognizing costs incurred for each extra unit.
Consistent customer-facing retail communication builds on coordinating messages across channels.
Channel incentives require distinguishing efforts directed at intermediaries from final-consumer demand generation.
Evaluating social commerce requires distinguishing customer actions from mere social exposure.
